behaviorNotes: The browser owns the top layer, ::backdrop, Escape ordering, background inertness and focus restoration; the app wrapper only adds controlled close, focus looping, backdrop pointer dismissal and scroll locking.

Escape is handled in the dialog keydown with stopPropagation + preventDefault, so native cancel is suppressed and Twin window shortcuts never see the event; the cancel listener only handles browser/AT-initiated close requests and keeps them controlled.
Scroll locking is reference-counted across nested dialogs with root-overflow restore and scrollbar-width compensation.

Production code calls showModal()/close() unconditionally: the earlier attribute/showModal fallbacks, manual focus-restore effect and redundant role/aria-modal attributes were removed. The missing jsdom dialog API is filled by tests/support/native-dialog.ts, which is test-only and not bundled.
Twin's window keydown handler is back to its base form: it no longer needs a defaultPrevented guard because the dialog consumes Escape before it reaches window.
ModalTitle remains the accessible-name seam through context + aria-labelledby, including asChild titles.
The portalContainer seam and both page-level container states were deleted: DOM ancestry now carries theme variables, and the Twin page keeps GPU rendering while the dialog is in the top layer.
residualRisks: jsdom 30 does not implement HTMLDialogElement.showModal/close; unit tests install a test-only polyfill (tests/support/native-dialog.ts) that mirrors open state, initial focus and focus restoration. No fallback branch remains in src/.
Cross-browser modal behavior (Safari/Firefox) was not re-run in this round.
The WebGPU Twin probe is headless Chrome with d3d11; the YMS tabs share the same Modal wrapper but were not separately browser-probed.
